figures_added.what: Real-life line graph for the taxi opener: cost against miles, plotting (0, £3) and (5, £13) joined by a straight line (y = 2x + 3). currentColor axes/labels, soft #60a5fa line, role=img with descriptive aria-label. Makes concrete the 'start cost = intercept, rate per mile = gradient' claim the opener text makes. Generated programmatically from the linear map px=40+miles*36, py=150-cost*8.

Coordinate grid for the two-point problem through (-2, 7) and (4, -5): axes through the origin, both named points plotted and joined by the line y = -2x + 3. Built programmatically from the problem's own coordinates via a fixed x/y-to-screen transform; the drawn segment's endpoints ARE the two plotted points, so the line passes through both exactly. Theme-safe currentColor text/axes, soft #60a5fa line.

notes: Equation-of-a-line is largely textual (equations and coordinates given in the prose), which SPEC_DIAGRAMS explicitly says is fine without a figure. Two figures added where the exam would actually print one: the real-life graph in the opener, and one coordinate grid on the two-point gold problem. Both SVGs are self-contained (no external refs, no scripts), theme-safe (all text and axes use currentColor, the line uses soft #60a5fa), under 1.5KB each, role=img with descriptive aria-label. Done in the same pass as the guided conversion. Every visible label cross-checked against the problem numbers and solutions.
